definitions.explanation: The quantity of matter in a body, a fundamental property in physics. Distinguished from weight, which varies with gravity. Composed of 質 (quality/substance) + 量 (quantity).

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{物体|ぶったい}→物体：13506_buttai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{質量|しつりょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧⟦キログラム→キログラム：02872_kiroguramu⟧だ。
examples.english: The mass of this object is five kilograms.

examples.japanese: ⟦{月|つき}→月：02230_tsuki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{重力|じゅうりょく}→重力：25301_juuryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{弱|よわ}い→弱い：00825_yowai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、{質量|しつりょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{変|か}わらない→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧。
examples.english: Gravity is weaker on the moon, but mass doesn't change.

examples.japanese: ⟦{太陽|たいよう}→太陽：03398_taiyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{質量|しつりょう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{地球|ちきゅう}→地球：03461_chikyuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{約|やく}→約：09563_yaku⟧{三十三万|さんじゅうさんまん}⟦{倍|ばい}→倍：01492_bai⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: The mass of the sun is about 330,000 times that of the earth.

notes:
USAGE:
{質量|しつりょう} is a scientific term used in physics, chemistry, and related fields. In everyday language, ⟦{重|おも}さ→重さ：14444_omosa⟧ (weight) is more commonly used, though technically {質量|しつりょう} and ⟦{重|おも}さ→重さ：14444_omosa⟧ are different concepts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {質量|しつりょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{測|はか}る→測る：01977_hakaru⟧ (measure the mass)
- ⟦{原子|げんし}→原子：10118_genshi⟧{質量|しつりょう} (atomic mass)
- {質量|しつりょう}⟦{保存|ほぞん}→保存：03626_hozon⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{法則|ほうそく}→法則：05143_housoku⟧ (law of conservation of mass)
- {質量|しつりょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{単位|たんい}→単位：03412_tani⟧ (unit of mass)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{重量|じゅうりょう}→重量：05475_juuryou⟧ means "weight" — the force exerted by gravity on an object. ⟦{体重|たいじゅう}→体重：03395_taijuu⟧ means "body weight." In everyday speech, ⟦{重|おも}さ→重さ：14444_omosa⟧ covers both mass and weight informally.
